posts.title: Summary post
posts.text: So what happened today? Where to start? The conference officially finished on Friday, but on Saturday dragged on with continually shelved promises of a new draft cover text. In the evening, parties were told that there would be a plenary early on Sunday morning and to head out for the night. The new texts were…
“Climate change does not follow our negotiating schedule,” said Cop president Murat Kurum. And with that, the final gavel has gone down. Meeting adjourned.

The youth NGOs have just taken the floor with some strong words for the presidency. “You have let us down,” they said. “We refuse to bear the consequences of your lack of ambition,” they said, adding that the summit resulted in “no ambition, no consensus, no future”. While Cop31 was meant to be an “implementation”…

Back in the UK there has been some reaction to an interview that the climate minister Miatta Fahnbulleh has done with the Sunday Times where she said: “[Rosebank’s oil] would be sold into global fossil fuel markets … We’re in the middle of an energy crisis where the conflict in the Middle East means that gas and oil…

Now the delegate for Ethiopia, which will be hosting next years Cop, has stood up to speak: she says that today the world has been reminded “that multilateralism requires determination”. “We are in difficult times but that difficulty is why Cop matters most … The UNFCCC remains the place where every country has a…

He is followed onto the dais by the UNFCCC chief Simon Stiell, who spoke to reporters outside shortly before. Stiell tells the plenary: “I share the disappoinment of many. Cop31 has been unable to agreee on both preseidency led decisions." Once again he emphasised where there has been progress. But, he said, “climate…

The Cop president Murat Kurum has now resumed the plenary, opening it with a very sincere apology to the Ghana delegation who accused him of cutting them off earlier. “Ghana is our friendly and brotherly country. I would like to ask their excellencies; such an attitude is by no means our attitude towards ghana and I…

posts.title: The consensus system fell short today, concedes UNFCCC chief
posts.text: Simon Stiell, the executive secretary of the UNFCCC, has just held a short press conference, where he emphasised that there had been many good outcomes of the conference but also acknowledged the issues. Asked whether the consensus based system which broke down today when several countries refused to endorse the cover…

Lord Nicholas Stern, who wrote a landmark economic review of the impact of climate change for the UK government back in 2006, is searching for the positives. He points out that there were also positive developments in Turkey and says: “We should now focus on the year ahead and work to strengthen shared commitment and…

Reaction to the failed cover decision and other key agenda points continues to pour in. Ann Harrison, climate justice policy advisor at Amnesty International, said: Countries from across regions were right to reject the colossal betrayal that the COP31 co-presidencies tried to pass off as climate action. They resisted…

Reaction is also coming in from scientists based in the UK. Prof Martin Siegert, University of Exeter, said: “This could be, strangely, good news for the climate process. A line has been drawn, where international agreement can only proceed if there is clear agreement that fossil fuels need to be transitioned away…

posts.title: 'Australia left nothing on the field,' says Cop co-president Chris Bowen
posts.text: Australia’s climate change minister, Chris Bowen, has just spoken to reporters outside the plenary room. He says he hasn’t slept for three days. “Unfortunately we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision and that’s very disappointing,” he said. “Ultimately looking back many parties who are people of good…

The UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres – right at the end of his term of office, has sent out a statement on the conference: “I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment…

Mohamed Adow, director of the thinktank Power Shift Africa, says, “This has been the worst ever COP and its collapse needs to be a wake up call for the world. Rich nations and polluting governments cannot keep arriving empty-handed and expecting a carefully worded declaration to get them off the hook. COP31 was a…

posts.title: Day 13 of Cop31 – recapped
posts.text: That’s all for today – we hope everyone following from Antalya gets a good night’s sleep. Here are the highlights from the 13th day of the 31st UN climate summit, which is still not over: Activists told the Presidency this summit could be one of the ‘most disappointing Cops’ ever Carbon removal must ‘be additional,…

“Today we have listened to you and sought to find common ground for your expectations,” said Murat Kurum, thanking the tired delegates for their “constructive approach”. He said the third and final version of the cover decision will be “in your hands shortly”, and parties will have until 6am local time to consider the…

Cop31 President, Murat Kurum, has arrived on the main stage, and has been immediately swarmed by delegates. The Turkish-Australian joint presidency has kept a low public profile today, on the first day of overtime, and the transparency they promised has been somewhat hard to come by for observers of the process.…
A handful of less controversial topics have indeed gone through without issue, and the session is taking a brief break before the Cop31 President arrives.

A dispute has broken about gender – and how it is defined – with interventions from Argentina and Paraguay. The draft document “encourages” a finance committee to enhance efforts to ensure gender-responsiveness in implementing its workplan, and requests Parties to consider gender balance and geographical…

Next up is a text on long-term climate finance, which has been rejected by the African Group. “This process did not provide sufficient space for negotiations,” said the negotiator for Ghana, speaking on the group’s behalf. “For now, it is not ready on our side for adoption.” The objection is to paragraph 3, which…

The plenary session has now actually begun, and we understood that it’s only the uncontroversial topics that are to be gaveled through. However, the very first topic, on climate empowerment – helping all members of society engage in climate action – has been met with an immediate objection from Russia that has drawn…

The Guardian has been leaked a submission that the countries calling themselves the “progressive coalition” – including the EU, UK and island and developing countries – want added to the cover text that is expected to be brought to a plenary at some point in the hours ahead. It is an eleventh-hour bid to bolster the…

The plenary has been pushed back by half an hour, into Sunday morning local time. Many diplomats have gone home, eager to get some rest before the (assumed) progress at the morning plenary session. Others are taking rest where they can find it.
The plenary session has just begun. A few weary-looking delegates have started to file in but the main stage has not yet been occupied …

Neither of these things are necessarily anything to brag about, but is Cop31 about to go down as both the biggest and the longest Cop in history? It is just after 11pm here in Antalya and we have been told that a plenary will commence at 11:30pm but that this will only deal with procedural issues. We are also getting…

Why does it matter if the Cop31 deal neglects to mention fossil fuels? Here’s a quick recap. The main purpose of these annual UN climate summits is to stop the planet from heating. When world leaders signed the Paris agreement at a Cop in 2015, they bound their countries to keeping global heating by the end of the…

Three of the world’s biggest carbon polluters agreed to boost oil production this week, during talks in China that appear to have been far more fruitful than the climate summit is shaping up to be. The fuel deal between the US, China and Russia was struck on Thursday in Shenzhen, China, just as diplomats attending…

A predicament “that never should have deteriorated so far” is how Jasper Inventor, head of the Greenpeace’s delegation, has described the current situation at Cop31, as weary delegates bemoan the lack of a new draft deal or clarity over the next steps. “The fact that no text has been distributed and no actual…
